Concept: Clean, separate stems put a defender in conflict on each side, and the quarterback learns to see spacing before anything fancy.
Notes: The starting point. Everybody runs a clean stem so you can see spacing before you add motion.

Concept: The corner route and the hitch stretch one defender high and low. Whatever he chooses, the other route is open.
Notes: Hitch under, corner over the top. High-low on the cornerback all day.

Concept: The go route pulls the deep defender out, and the dig settles in the hole he left behind the underneath coverage.
Notes: Clear it out with the go, then drop the dig in behind the linebacker.

Concept: Fast rushers run themselves out of the play. A quick throw to the back with two blockers in front turns their aggression into yards.
Notes: Quick out to the back with both receivers stalking. Easy completion when they rush hard.

Concept: Four receivers spread across the field make the defense cover every inch. The widest gap shows up on the snap.
Notes: Four across the field. Find the widest defender and throw away from him.

Concept: Three receivers at three depths on one side outnumber the two defenders who can cover it.
Notes: Three levels to the right side: flat, out, corner. Read it high to low.

Concept: Inside-breaking slants beat outside leverage before the coverage can react. The ball is out in one beat.
Notes: Both sides slant inside. Snap, one step, throw — this is your two-minute answer.

Concept: Crossing receivers run defenders into each other. Man coverage gets picked off, and zone has to pass two men at once.
Notes: Two drags crossing at four yards. Somebody comes free every single time.

Concept: Bunched receivers can't be pressed cleanly, and their releases make man defenders sort out who takes whom.
Notes: Three tight to the right. The stack alone beats man coverage before anyone moves.

Concept: Three levels out of one cluster force one defender to cover two routes. The quarterback throws to whichever he leaves.
Notes: Flat, corner and seam out of the same cluster. Pick the level the defense leaves open.

Concept: The inside receiver's release screens the defender trailing the outside man, so he comes free underneath.
Notes: The inside man sets the rub, the outside man releases clean underneath him.

Concept: Defenders who chase the first break get caught moving the wrong way when one receiver comes back to the ball.
Notes: Everybody breaks out, one comes back. Great on a defense that chases hard.

Concept: Trips pulls coverage to the three-man side, which leaves the single receiver alone on the backside.
Notes: Three to the right, one isolated left. Count the defenders and take the free side.

Concept: The flat, out and corner put three receivers on two zone defenders. Somebody is always uncovered.
Notes: Classic three-level flood to the trips side. First read is the flat.

Concept: The crosser runs away from man coverage and settles in the open middle against zone. The trips side clears the way.
Notes: Send the inside man all the way across. He clears the middle at twelve yards.

Concept: The ball gets outside before the defense can flow, with numbers on the edge to block.
Notes: Snap and pitch it wide. Two blockers in front of the ball on the edge.

Concept: Stacked receivers can't be jammed at the line, and the defense must declare who covers whom before the snap.
Notes: Stacked releases. Nobody can press what they cannot reach.

Concept: Three receivers on the same track at different depths give the quarterback a window at every level of the zone.
Notes: Three depths on the same track: five, ten, fifteen. Throw to the open window.

Concept: The outs pull the underneath defenders to the sideline, and the wheel runs up behind them before the deep help arrives.
Notes: Inside man takes the wheel up the sideline behind the two outs.

Concept: The vertical route carries the safety away, and the dig fills the space he left behind the linebackers.
Notes: Clear the safety, then fill the space he left with the dig.

Concept: With two receivers on one side and a back on the other, the quarterback has one simple read each way.
Notes: Two right, one back left. The simplest read in the book.

Concept: The slant and the flat stretch the same underneath defender horizontally. He can only take one of them.
Notes: Slant and flat off the same side. If the linebacker jumps the slant, hit the flat.

Concept: The post holds the deep defender inside, and the wheel attacks the sideline behind the underneath coverage.
Notes: Inside man to the post, back on the wheel underneath him. Two deep answers.

Concept: The curl sits in the gap of a soft zone, and the flat pulls the defender who would undercut it.
Notes: Curl at ten, flat at three. The standard beater against soft zone.

Concept: The stack protects the outside receiver from press, and the defense has to show its rules before the snap.
Notes: Stack the twins so the outside man never gets touched off the line.

Concept: The front receiver's route is a legal rub. The back receiver crosses under his teammate and loses his defender.
Notes: Front man sits, back man releases across his face. Legal rub, open man.

Concept: Two vertical routes from one spot put one deep defender in conflict. He can't stay on top of both.
Notes: Both stacked receivers straight up the field. Take the one the safety leaves.

Concept: The corner and post cross at depth, so defenders who pass receivers off lose one in the switch.
Notes: Corner and post crossing at fifteen. Hardest thing in the book to cover deep.
